quests.instruction: You believe your team can still win, even though you are behind at halftime. How do you feel?
quests.question: Optimistic
quests.hint: Believing things can still turn out well, even when it looks tough, feels bright and hopeful.
quests.explanation: Believing things can still turn out well, even when it looks tough, gives you a bright, hopeful outlook.
quests.funFact: Coaches often say believing a comeback is possible is the first step toward making one happen!

quests.instruction: Your little cousin keeps humming the same song over and over. How do you feel?
quests.question: Irritated
quests.hint: A small, repeated sound that will not stop can make you want to sigh.
quests.explanation: A small, repeated sound that will not stop can give you a mildly annoyed feeling.
quests.funFact: Asking politely for a break from a repeated sound is a simple way to solve this feeling.

quests.instruction: You unwrap the exact toy you had been hoping for all year. How do you feel?
quests.question: Delighted
quests.hint: Getting exactly what you had been wishing for can bring a big, bright smile.
quests.explanation: Getting exactly what you had been wishing for fills you with a bright, joyful feeling.
quests.funFact: The joy of getting a long-wished-for gift often feels even bigger because of the wait!

quests.instruction: You are the first one to volunteer when your teacher asks for helpers. How do you feel?
quests.question: Eager
quests.hint: Wanting to jump in and help right away feels ready and bouncy.
quests.explanation: Wanting to jump in and help right away fills you with ready, willing energy.
quests.funFact: Volunteering quickly is often a sign of this eager, ready-to-help feeling!

quests.instruction: You watch snow fall silently outside your window. How do you feel?
quests.question: Peaceful
quests.hint: Watching something soft and silent drift slowly down can feel deeply calm.
quests.explanation: Watching something soft and silent drift slowly down gives you a deeply calm feeling.
quests.funFact: Falling snow actually muffles outside sound, making the world feel even quieter!

quests.instruction: You cannot stop wondering whether you packed the right things for your trip. How do you feel?
quests.question: Anxious
quests.hint: Double-checking your thoughts again and again before a trip can feel restless.
quests.explanation: Double-checking your thoughts again and again before a trip can give you a restless, unsettled feeling.
quests.funFact: A simple packing list is a great tool to help settle this kind of restless, checking feeling.

quests.instruction: You are humming quietly while you water your plants on a lazy Sunday. How do you feel?
quests.question: Content
quests.hint: A slow, simple task with nowhere to rush to can feel quietly satisfying.
quests.explanation: A slow, simple task with nowhere to rush to gives you a quiet, satisfied feeling.
quests.funFact: Simple routines like watering plants can be a small, steady source of calm satisfaction!

quests.instruction: You keep trying to whistle a tune but it never sounds quite right. How do you feel?
quests.question: Frustrated
quests.hint: Practicing something again and again without it sounding right can feel very stuck.
quests.explanation: Practicing something again and again without it sounding right can give you a frustrated feeling.
quests.funFact: Whistling a full tune takes a lot of small muscle control — it often improves with steady practice!

quests.instruction: You send in your entry for the talent show and wait eagerly to hear back. How do you feel?
quests.question: Hopeful
quests.hint: Wishing for good news about a talent you shared can give you a light, eager feeling.
quests.explanation: Wishing for good news about a talent you bravely shared gives you a light, eager, wishing feeling.
quests.funFact: Signing up for a talent show already takes courage, no matter what the final answer turns out to be!

quests.instruction: You have rehearsed your dance routine so many times you barely need the mirror. How do you feel?
quests.question: Confident
quests.hint: Knowing every move so well that you barely need to think about it feels sure and steady.
quests.explanation: Knowing every move so well that you barely need to think about it makes you feel sure and steady.
quests.funFact: Dancers call this 'muscle memory' — practiced moves that your body remembers on its own!

quests.instruction: You believe tomorrow's weather will be perfect for the class picnic. How do you feel?
quests.question: Optimistic
quests.hint: Believing good things are coming, even before you know for sure, feels bright and hopeful.
quests.explanation: Believing good things are coming, even before you know for sure, gives you a bright, hopeful outlook.
quests.funFact: A hopeful outlook does not change the weather, but it can make the wait feel much more fun!

quests.instruction: Someone keeps kicking the back of your chair on the bus. How do you feel?
quests.question: Irritated
quests.hint: A small, repeated bump you did not ask for can make you sigh with annoyance.
quests.explanation: A small, repeated bump you did not ask for can give you a mildly annoyed feeling.
quests.funFact: A polite 'could you please stop?' usually solves this kind of small bus mix-up quickly.

quests.instruction: You get to pick any book you want at the book fair. How do you feel?
quests.question: Delighted
quests.hint: Having a whole table of exciting choices just for you can bring a big, bright smile.
quests.explanation: Having a whole table of exciting choices just for you fills you with a bright, joyful feeling.
quests.funFact: Book fairs let kids pick their very own stories — a joyful way to build a love of reading!

quests.instruction: You raise your hand first, hoping to be picked to answer the question. How do you feel?
quests.question: Eager
quests.hint: Wanting to jump right into something can make you sit right up on the edge of your seat.
quests.explanation: Wanting to jump right into something makes you sit up, ready and ready-to-go.
quests.funFact: This bouncy, ready feeling often happens just before we get to try something we enjoy!

quests.instruction: You lie in a field of grass with the wind moving softly around you. How do you feel?
quests.question: Peaceful
quests.hint: Resting still outdoors with only gentle wind around you feels deeply calm.
quests.explanation: Resting still outdoors with only gentle wind around you gives you a deeply calm feeling.
quests.funFact: The gentle sound of wind through grass is a favorite relaxing sound for many people!

quests.instruction: You keep thinking about your first day at a new club, even a whole week early. How do you feel?
quests.question: Anxious
quests.hint: Your mind jumping ahead to something new, again and again, can feel restless.
quests.explanation: Your mind jumping ahead to something new, again and again, can give you a restless, unsettled feeling.
quests.funFact: Writing down what you are excited and unsure about can help settle a restless mind before something new.

quests.instruction: You finish organizing your bookshelf and sit back to admire it. How do you feel?
quests.question: Content
quests.hint: Looking at a small, finished task with nothing left to do can feel quietly satisfying.
quests.explanation: Looking at a small, finished task with nothing left to do gives you a quiet, satisfied feeling.
quests.funFact: Organizing small spaces is a simple activity that many people find calming and satisfying!

quests.instruction: Your remote control car keeps steering the wrong way no matter what you do. How do you feel?
quests.question: Frustrated
quests.hint: A toy that will not cooperate no matter how many times you try can feel very stuck.
quests.explanation: A toy that will not cooperate no matter how many times you try can give you a stuck, frustrated feeling.
quests.funFact: Checking the batteries is often the first easy fix for a remote control that will not behave!

quests.instruction: You are waiting to hear if the animal shelter found a home for the puppy you loved. How do you feel?
quests.question: Hopeful
quests.hint: Wishing for good news about someone you cared about can feel light and eager.
quests.explanation: Wishing for good news about someone you cared about gives you a light, wishing feeling.
quests.funFact: Animal shelters often share happy updates about pets that find loving new homes!

quests.instruction: You know your locker combination so well that you can open it without looking. How do you feel?
quests.question: Confident
quests.hint: Knowing something so well it becomes automatic can make you feel sure of yourself.
quests.explanation: Knowing something so well it becomes automatic makes you feel sure and capable.
quests.funFact: Repeating a small action daily, like opening a locker, is one of the fastest ways to master it!

quests.instruction: You believe your plan will work out, even though the first try did not go perfectly. How do you feel?
quests.question: Optimistic
quests.hint: Believing things will improve after a rough first try feels bright and hopeful.
quests.explanation: Believing things will improve after a rough first try gives you a bright, hopeful outlook.
quests.funFact: Most inventors say their very first try at anything rarely works — believing it will improve keeps them going!

quests.instruction: A fly keeps buzzing around your head while you try to eat lunch. How do you feel?
quests.question: Irritated
quests.hint: A small, buzzing distraction that will not leave you alone can make you want to swat the air.
quests.explanation: A small, buzzing distraction that will not leave you alone can give you a mildly annoyed feeling.
quests.funFact: Flies are drawn to food smells — covering your food can help keep this annoyance away!

quests.instruction: Your favorite cousin surprises you with a visit you did not expect. How do you feel?
quests.question: Delighted
quests.hint: Seeing someone you love appear out of nowhere can bring a big, bright smile.
quests.explanation: Seeing someone you love appear out of nowhere fills you with a bright, joyful feeling.
quests.funFact: Surprise visits from people we love are one of life's most joyful little moments!

quests.instruction: You wake up before your alarm on the morning of the school trip. How do you feel?
quests.question: Eager
quests.hint: Being too ready for the day ahead to stay asleep feels bouncy and excited.
quests.explanation: Being too ready for the day ahead to stay asleep is a sign of bouncy, eager energy.
quests.funFact: This ready feeling can sometimes even wake your body up before an alarm does!

quests.instruction: You read in a hammock strung between two quiet trees. How do you feel?
quests.question: Peaceful
quests.hint: Resting slowly outdoors with nothing to rush toward feels deeply calm.
quests.explanation: Resting slowly outdoors with nothing to rush toward gives you a deeply calm, settled feeling.
quests.funFact: The gentle sway of a hammock is a favorite way many people relax outdoors!

quests.instruction: You believe your handmade gift will turn out wonderfully, even partway through making it. How do you feel?
quests.question: Optimistic
quests.hint: Believing your work will turn out well, even before it is finished, feels bright and hopeful.
quests.explanation: Believing your work will turn out well, even before it is finished, gives you a bright, hopeful outlook.
quests.funFact: Believing in your own project often helps you stick with it until it is truly finished!

quests.instruction: Your little brother keeps asking you the same question again and again. How do you feel?
quests.question: Irritated
quests.hint: Hearing the exact same thing repeated over and over can make you sigh.
quests.explanation: Hearing the exact same thing repeated over and over can give you a mildly annoyed feeling.
quests.funFact: Younger kids often repeat questions because they are still learning — a patient answer usually helps!

quests.instruction: Your whole class cheers when you finish your project. How do you feel?
quests.question: Delighted
quests.hint: Hearing everyone celebrate something you made can bring a big, bright smile.
quests.explanation: Hearing everyone celebrate something you made fills you with a bright, joyful feeling.
quests.funFact: Cheering together as a class is a wonderful way to share in each other's joyful moments!

quests.instruction: You ask your coach if you can practice even before the whistle blows. How do you feel?
quests.question: Eager
quests.hint: Not wanting to wait to get started on something you enjoy feels ready and bouncy.
quests.explanation: Not wanting to wait to get started on something you enjoy fills you with ready energy.
quests.funFact: Coaches often love seeing this ready-to-start feeling in players before practice begins!

quests.instruction: You walk slowly through a quiet forest trail early in the morning. How do you feel?
quests.question: Peaceful
quests.hint: Walking slowly with nothing rushing you through a quiet natural place feels deeply calm.
quests.explanation: Walking slowly through a quiet natural place gives you a deeply calm, settled feeling.
quests.funFact: Time spent slowly in nature has been shown to help both kids and grown-ups feel calmer!
